items.title: OpenAI Codex 团队成员解释 6.2 Sol/Astra 评测视频与现场反馈的差异
items.description: Tibo 解释 6.2 Sol/Astra 上评测视频与现场人群反馈氛围不同的原因：部分人较早获得访问权限，而团队在过去 3-4 天做了大量改动，视频是上周制作的，之后大概率没有重新测试。他称这两个模型相比 GPT 前代有明显提升，但仍不完美，团队希望在后续迭代的品味和使用体验上改进，并表示欢迎反馈。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/sah26a5ofgvrxd76bgj9t77wf

items.title: Nvidia 临时 CEO Colette Kress 表示董事会不会恢复黄仁勋的 CEO 职务
items.description: Nvidia 临时 CEO Colette Kress 在 Jim Cramer 的节目上表示，董事会已决定不会恢复黄仁勋（Jensen）的 CEO 职务，称这就是董事会的决定和官方声明。此前董事 Harvey Jones 在昨天的首次财报电话会上表示，董事会一致接受其辞职且无意让其复任。完整采访见 CNBC Mad Money，完整视频见 CNBC Television YouTube 频道。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/znj4uw6kr9vt4uij9fmao9p00
items.author: noreply@aihot.news (Rohan Paul)

items.title: Semafor：部分 Nvidia 董事仍推动让黄仁勋回归，尽管董事长否认
items.description: Semafor 报道称，尽管 Nvidia 董事长 Harvey Jones 表示董事会一致接受黄仁勋的辞职且无意让他复任 CEO，部分董事仍在推动其回归。黄仁勋在周二财报发布前与至少 1 名董事讨论过回归事宜；该投票仅针对辞职本身，Nvidia 章程允许剩余 10 名董事以简单多数任命 CEO 而无需股东投票。另有董事将人选范围缩小至 Arm CEO Rene Haas 和 Marvell CEO Matt Murphy 等候选人。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ad6k5zphfq44bxu1y7tb8t0ng

items.description: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据路透社今天（19 日）上午报道，随着 AI 初创企业 Anthropic 的上市，数千名现任和前员工有望 凭借手中的公司股票成为百万美元富翁 ，就算这些财富暂时还停留在账面上也无妨。此次 IPO 有望成为硅谷历史上规模最大的员工造富事件之一。 Anthropic 的员工有望迎来巨额财富增长，受益者不仅包括早期研究人员和工程师，还包括获得股权激励的行政人员。 Anthropic 招股书披露了员工股权奖励的整体价值，却没有说明这些财富具体如何分配，因此外界对于员工能够获得多少财富，估算结果差异很大。 旧金山非上市公司股权交易平台 Hill 预计，Anthropic 上市后， 将有 598 名非创始人员工的持股价值分别达到至少 1 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.68 亿元人民币） 。Hill CEO 安德鲁 · 本森说：“很多人都希望自己持有的股权能够增值到足以改变人生的程度。没有比这更好的结果了。” 本森认为，Anthropic 早期员工可能比临近上市时才加入的高管赚得更多：“那些最初只是基层员工的人，最终获得的财务回报，实际上应该比上市前才加入

items.title: 3.4 万日元：哈曼卡顿发布 Allure 2 音箱，经典透明设计、60W 功率
items.description: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，哈曼卡顿现已在日本市场推出 Allure 2 家用音箱。新品延续 SoundSticks 经典透明设计， 建议零售价 34,100 日元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,429 元人民币） ，11 月 26 日起出货。 据介绍，这款音箱配备 3 个 1.5 英寸扬声器单元，以及 3.5 英寸低音单元，总功率可达 60W，频响范围为 40Hz 至 20kHz (-6dB)，信噪比 80dB(A)。 同时这款音箱支持 AI Sound Boost 技术，可进一步优化声音输出，让音效更加饱满。该机兼容蓝牙 5.4 技术，最多可同时连接 2 台手机。用户可以将两台 Allure 2 音箱连接起来，构建更宽广的立体声场。当然也可以使用 Auracast 广播技术，让 2 台以上 Allure 2 同步播放音乐。 此外，这款音箱还具备 360° 炫彩光效，可通过 Harman Kardon One 应用程序调整灯光效果、均衡器和其他设置。 IT之家注意到，该音箱已经在国内的部分 Apple 授权专营店展出，但官方零售价并没有公布。

items.title: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report
items.description: One Wall Street analyst got to the bottom of Nvidia's surprise announcement that it wouldn't be filing its formal quarterly results document, the 10-Q, for weeks.
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: During Nvidia’s quarterly call on Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress dropped this little oddity: She said Nvidia wouldn’t be immediately filing its quarterly results report, known as a 10-Q, with the SEC. “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks.” And she offered no reason why. The delay was widely noticed. Among the many comments on X about it , economic and investment analyst Edward Dowd called it a “red flag.” Nvidia has typically filed the 10-Q the same day it reports results. The 10-Q offers far more detail about a company’s operations than an earnings press release, including sections that disclose “legal proceedings,” which include lawsuits that could affect the company; and “risk factors,” which cover other potentially business-impairing items. The announcement of the delay was so unusual that UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked about it after the public earnings call. Nvidia told him the delay was related to whether the company would need to disclose additional information about its ongoing investigation into Huang in the 10-Q. “The company announced that the 10-Q will be filed ‘in the coming weeks’ – later than usual. When queried on our callback, management indicated this was related to the ongoing investigation and whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing,” Arcuri wrote in his research note. items.title: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’
items.description: The Anduril co-founder says outdated technology is leaving systems vulnerable to a new wave of AI-enabled attacks.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, Palmer Luckey warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Addressing the recent spate of tech outages, the Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder argued that older systems are struggling to keep pace with the new hacking capabilities enabled by AI and warned it was time to quicken the pace of securing our defenses. “We’re seeing the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools allowing for the creation of various exploits,” he said. While government officials largely attributed the latest set of technical issues to companies rushing to patch their systems to protect against the new vulnerabilities AI has discovered, Luckey focused on the underlying security challenges facing organizations using outdated technology. Luckey explained that U.S. adversaries are currently exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and our defense capabilities. These attacks are being carried out for both strategic and financial reasons, and North Korea was particularly involved, he added. The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, noted that U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance had canceled his appearance at the Times’ conference this week because of the recent tech outages, saying he now had to attend meetings about the matter. Given the situation, Sorkin asked Luckey how worried we should be about all this.

items.description: "It makes America weaker to knock him out," the Anduril CEO said about ousted Nvidia leader Jensen Huang.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey thinks Nvidia’s board is giving China exactly what it wants by removing the company’s longtime CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang. Nvidia, the leading semiconductor designer whose chips power much of the AI industry, is undergoing a critical, unexpected leadership change. Huang, who led the company for 33 years, stepped down last week amid several controversies , including his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy who has been investigated for possibly smuggling Nvidia chips into China to circumvent U.S. export restrictions. “China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. items.title: Sam Altman says his life is so weird that he’s unfazed by Andrew Garfield portraying him in upcoming movie
items.description: "It doesn't feel like it's in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life," Altman said.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Hollywood has found plenty of material and cinematic inspiration from a string of Silicon Valley scandals and power struggles in recent years. “ You Can See Everything ,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, smashed box office expectations, and Netflix’s limited series “The Altruists” comes out Thursday to tell the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the downfall of FTX. As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either. In “Artificial,” a biographical comedy-drama opening in theaters on Christmas, the lauded actor Andrew Garfield will portray Altman in a film that chronicles OpenAI’s rise and the internal turmoil that erupted when he was briefly ousted in 2023. “If you had told me 20 years ago that someone was going to make a movie about me, I think that would have struck me as … that would have been a very weird thing,” Altman said onstage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. “Now it doesn’t feel like it’s in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life.” Garfield is best known for his role as Spider-Man, but his big break came in 2010, when he played Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin in “The Social Network” alongside Jesse Eisenberg as Mark Zuckerberg. items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: Snapchat announced on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let users alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera. The company is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool , which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile. Easy Lens CLI brings that same idea into developers’ existing workflows, allowing AI assistants to handle the technical work while creators focus on the vision for the Lens itself. The launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants. Instead of  requiring creators to learn how to use Snapchat’s own development tools, the company is bringing Lens creation into the AI coding workflows they already use, which could in turn expand the pool of people who build for Snapchat. items.title: Google’s AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode
items.description: Google's new temporary threads let users have conversations in AI Mode without adding them to their search history or influencing future recommendations.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: Google’s search engine has long offered an incognito mode for all those search queries you don’t want logged or associated with your account. Now, Google’s AI Mode in Search is getting a similar feature. In a blog post , the company announced a new feature that brings “temporary threads” to AI Mode, where the conversations you have won’t be resurfaced later in areas like your search history or recommendations. Many leading AI chatbots already offer the option for temporary chats, Google Gemini included. However, there was not yet an option to have a temporary chat when you’re searching Google and are dropped into its conversational interface, known as AI Mode. Google says that users won’t have to adjust their settings to take advantage of the new option. Instead, they’ll be able to click a temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode to engage in a temporary chat. This essentially works the same as a temporary chat would in the stand-alone Gemini chatbot. The option could be convenient to use at those times when you start digging deeper into a particular topic via AI Mode and realize that you don’t want the discussion to become a part of your search history because of its personal nature. Once the temporary thread is started, the session becomes detached from your account, Google says. items.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
items.description: Citi is the latest major financial institution to put the breaks on personal finance AI agents.
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked. AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments. But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants. “As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.” JPMorgan and Bank of America , the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. items.title: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots
items.description: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman pushed back against Silicon Valley's growing debate over an AI takeover, while acknowledging the challenges of keeping advanced models under human control.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman believes that people should stay in charge of the future when it comes to how AI technology impacts the world and everyone’s lives. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the AI executive referred to discussions in Silicon Valley about whether there will be a gradual handover to AI — meaning AI will eventually become the decision-making authority across every major industry and institution. “One thing we’ve been talking a lot about recently is there’s been this thing in Silicon Valley that seems almost ridiculous to have to fight against, but we both believe very deeply that people need to stay in control of the future, and there’s increasing talk about, well, there is either going to be or there should be this sort of gradual handover to AI. And I — we both — agree that that’s a terrible idea,” said Altman, who was sharing the stage with OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman. The hand-off theory stems from the idea that as AI models become increasingly more powerful, they will learn to improve themselves — a concept known as “recursive self-improvement” or RSI. As existing AI technology builds newer, smarter generations, those will eventually become a superintelligence that humans can no longer control, the belief goes.
